about: Reads a WAV file with all its channels and its sample rate

params.about: File path; a relative path is resolved against the pipeline's folder
params.name: path

title: WAV

about: A signal from numbers typed by hand; channels are separated by a bar |

params.about: Sample values separated by spaces, commas or semicolons; channels are separated by a bar |, e.g. 1 2 3 | 4 5 6
params.name: values

params.about: Sample rate, Hz: how many samples make one second
params.name: rate

title: Samples

about: Adds or subtracts two signals sample by sample; the shorter is zero-padded

params.about: Operation on the inputs: a + b or a − b
params.name: op

title: Adder ⊕

about: Test signals: tone, sweep, impulse, noise, Donoho–Johnstone signals

params.about: Which signal to make; it decides which of the other parameters apply
params.name: kind

values.blocks: Donoho–Johnstone Blocks: piecewise constant with jumps
values.bumps: Donoho–Johnstone Bumps: sharp peaks on a zero baseline
values.doppler: Donoho–Johnstone Doppler: an oscillation whose period grows
values.harmonics: tone at freq plus overtones 2f, 3f, 4f at a, a/2, a/4, a/8
values.heavisine: Donoho–Johnstone HeaviSine: a sine with two jumps
values.impulse: unit impulse at the first sample, zeros after it
values.pink: pink 1/f noise; amplitude is its RMS, seed picks the draw
values.sine: sine at freq with peak amplitude
values.step: unit step: ones from the first sample on
values.sweep: logarithmic sweep from freq to f1 at amplitude 1
values.white: white Gaussian noise; amplitude is its RMS, seed picks the draw

params.about: Frequency, Hz: of the tone and the harmonics' fundamental, start of the sweep
params.name: freq

params.about: End frequency of the sweep, Hz; the other kinds ignore it
params.name: f1

params.about: Amplitude (RMS for noise); sweep, impulse and step ignore it
params.name: amplitude

params.about: Sample rate, Hz; frequencies above half of it alias
params.name: rate

params.about: Signal length, s
params.name: duration

params.about: Noise generator seed: the same seed gives the same noise; white and pink only
params.name: seed

title: Generator

about: Scales the signal by a constant factor given in decibels

params.about: Gain, dB: +6 roughly doubles the amplitude, negative values attenuate
params.name: db

title: Gain

about: Scales each channel to a target peak or RMS level

params.about: Which level to match: the peak or the RMS
params.name: kind

values.rms: the RMS value is set to target_dbfs

params.about: Target level in dB relative to full scale (0 dBFS is amplitude 1.0)
params.name: target_dbfs

title: Normalize

about: Subtracts each channel's mean, removing the DC component
title: Remove DC

about: Hard-clips samples to ±limit

params.about: Clipping level: anything beyond ±limit is cut to it
params.name: limit

title: Clip

about: Quantises the signal to a given bit depth, optionally with dither

params.about: Bit depth: fewer bits mean a coarser step and louder quantisation noise
params.name: bits

params.about: Whether to add triangular (TPDF) noise before rounding
params.name: dither

values.no: plain rounding: the error follows the signal and sounds like distortion
values.yes: TPDF dither: the error becomes steady noise unrelated to the signal

params.about: Dither generator seed; channel c uses seed + c
params.name: seed

title: Quantize

about: μ-law companding: compresses or expands the dynamic range

params.about: Direction: compress (encode) or expand (decode)
params.name: direction

values.decode: expand: the inverse map, restoring the original scale
values.encode: compress: y = sign(x)·ln(1 + μ|x|)/ln(1 + μ), input clipped to ±1

params.about: The μ parameter: larger values squeeze loud samples harder relative to quiet ones
params.name: mu

title: μ-law

about: Splits a signal into left and right, or picks out one channel

params.about: What goes to outputs l and r
params.name: mode

values.channel: both outputs get the channel numbered channel
values.lr: l gets channel 0, r channel 1 (mono feeds channel 0 to both)

params.about: Zero-based channel number for mode channel
params.name: channel

title: Channels

about: Mixes all channels into one by averaging them
title: To mono

about: Rotates stereo between L/R and M/S: M = (L + R)/√2, S = (L − R)/√2

params.about: Direction; the rotation is orthogonal, hence lossless
params.name: direction

values.decode: M/S → L/R: recovers left and right
values.encode: L/R → M/S: channel 0 becomes mid, channel 1 side

title: M/S

about: Delays the signal by prepending zeros

params.about: Delay in samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
params.name: samples

title: Delay

about: Reverses the signal in time: the last sample comes first
title: Reverse

about: Keeps the part of the signal in [begin, end)

params.about: Start of the part, inclusive: samples, or seconds with an s suffix (0.01s)
params.name: begin

params.about: End of the piece, excluded; 0 means to the end of the signal. Samples or seconds with s (0.01s)
params.name: end

title: Cut

about: Downsampling ↓M: keeps every M-th sample, optionally removing aliasing first

params.about: Downsampling factor M: the sample rate is divided by M
params.name: m

params.about: Alias suppression of the Kaiser filter, dB: more is cleaner but the filter is longer
params.name: attenuation_db

params.about: Whether to low-pass at fs/(2M) before dropping samples
params.name: anti_alias

values.no: just every M-th sample: content above fs/(2M) folds onto low frequencies
values.yes: Kaiser low-pass first, then every M-th sample: no aliasing

params.about: Downsampling offset: p keeps x[p], x[p+M], …; must be below M
params.name: phase

title: Downsample ↓M

about: Upsampling ↑M: inserts M−1 zeros between samples, optionally removing images

params.about: Upsampling factor M: the sample rate is multiplied by M
params.name: m

params.about: Image suppression of the Kaiser filter, dB: more is cleaner but the filter is longer
params.name: attenuation_db

params.about: Whether to low-pass the zero-stuffed signal to remove spectral images
params.name: anti_image

values.no: zero stuffing only: the spectrum keeps M−1 images
values.yes: Kaiser low-pass with gain M: a smooth interpolation of the input

title: Upsample ↑M

about: Changes the rate by L/M: upsample ↑L, low-pass, downsample ↓M

params.about: Upsampling factor L, the numerator of the rate ratio
params.name: l

params.about: Downsampling factor M, the denominator: the new rate is fs·L/M
params.name: m

params.about: Image and alias suppression of the Kaiser filters, dB: more is cleaner but longer
params.name: attenuation_db

title: Resample L/M

about: Full convolution with a bank or library filter: output length N + L − 1

params.about: Filter as wavelet.role: h0/h1 analysis low/high-pass, f0/f1 synthesis; or a library name
params.name: filter

params.about: How to compute it; results match up to rounding
params.name: method

values.auto: FFT when both operands are at least 160 samples long, else direct
values.direct: direct sum of products, O(N·L): faster for short filters
values.fft: via FFT, O((N+L) log(N+L)): faster for long filters

title: Convolution

about: Discrete wavelet transform: multilevel split into bands aJ, dJ…d1

params.about: Wavelet name (haar, db4, sym8, coif3, bior2.2, dmey…): sets the filter bank
params.name: wavelet

params.about: Number of levels J; 0 picks the maximum for this length minus 3, at least 1
params.name: levels

params.about: How the signal is extended beyond its edges; this sets the band lengths
params.name: ext

values.antireflect: point reflection about the edge sample: x[−n] = 2x0 − x[n]
values.antisymmetric: mirror with a sign flip: … −x1 −x0 | x0 x1 …
values.reflect: mirror without repeating the edge: … x2 x1 | x0 x1 x2 …
values.smooth: linear extrapolation from the two edge samples
values.symmetric: mirror repeating the edge: … x1 x0 | x0 x1 …

title: DWT

about: Inverse DWT: rebuilds the signal from bands aJ, dJ…d1

params.about: Synthesis wavelet: auto reuses the analysis one; any other name must match it
params.name: wavelet

params.about: Edge extension: auto reuses the analysis mode; any other value must match it
params.name: ext

values.antireflect: point reflection about the edge sample: x[−n] = 2x0 − x[n]
values.antisymmetric: mirror with a sign flip: … −x1 −x0 | x0 x1 …
values.auto: use the mode stored with the coefficients
values.reflect: mirror without repeating the edge: … x2 x1 | x0 x1 x2 …
values.smooth: linear extrapolation from the two edge samples
values.symmetric: mirror repeating the edge: … x1 x0 | x0 x1 …

title: IDWT

about: Stationary (undecimated) wavelet transform: every band keeps the signal length

params.about: Wavelet name (haar, db4, sym8, coif3, bior2.2, dmey…): sets the filter bank
params.name: wavelet

params.about: Number of levels J; 0 picks it; the signal is periodically padded to a multiple of 2^J
params.name: levels

params.about: Whether to divide the filters by √2 so band energy equals signal energy
params.name: norm

values.no: DWT filters as is (as in pywt): energy doubles at every level
values.yes: filters ×1/√2: the total band energy equals the signal energy

title: SWT

about: 5/3 (LeGall, JPEG 2000) wavelet via lifting: multilevel decomposition

params.about: Number of levels; the signal needs at least 2^levels samples
params.name: levels

params.about: Whether to compute in integers, the reversible lossless JPEG 2000 variant
params.name: integer

values.no: floating-point lifting: perfect reconstruction up to rounding
values.yes: samples ×32768 to integers, integer lifting: 16-bit PCM comes back exactly

title: Lifting 5/3

about: Inverse 5/3 lifting: rebuilds the signal from lift53 bands, real or integer
title: Inverse lifting 5/3

about: Inverse SWT: rebuilds the signal from the bands, trimmed to the input length

params.about: Synthesis wavelet: auto reuses the SWT one; any other name must match it
params.name: wavelet

title: ISWT

about: Thresholds wavelet coefficients: shrinks the details by a rule

params.about: How the threshold λ is chosen per level; the approximation is left alone
params.name: rule

values.bayes: BayesShrink: λ = σ²/σx per level, adapts to the signal
values.minimax: Donoho–Johnstone minimax threshold: milder than the universal one
values.sure: SureShrink: λ minimises Stein's unbiased risk estimate per level
values.visu: VisuShrink: λ = σ√(2 ln N), removes nearly all noise but oversmooths

params.about: Shrinkage function: how coefficients change relative to λ
params.name: mode

values.garrote: non-negative garrote: y − λ²/y when |y| > λ, between soft and hard
values.hard: hard: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest kept; less bias, more residual noise
values.soft: soft: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest shrink by λ; smooth but biased

params.about: Which detail levels to process: J or J1..J2; 1 is the finest, d1
params.name: levels

params.about: Noise level σ: mad_d1 estimates it as median|d1|/0.6745, or give a number
params.name: sigma

title: Threshold

about: Edits decomposition bands: mutes some and changes the gain of the rest

params.about: Bands to keep, comma-separated (a, d1, d3) or all; the others are zeroed
params.name: enabled

params.about: Band gains in dB, comma-separated, like d2=-6, a=3; other bands stay as is

title: Band edit

about: Report: the share of energy in each band, per channel
title: Band energy

about: Envelope: magnitude of the analytic signal (Hilbert transform)

about: Instantaneous frequency, Hz: derivative of the analytic signal's phase
title: Instantaneous frequency

about: Real cepstrum: inverse FFT of the log magnitude spectrum
title: Cepstrum

about: Type-II discrete cosine transform of each channel
title: DCT-II

about: Inverse DCT (DCT-III): recovers the signal from DCT-II coefficients
title: Inverse DCT

values.same: the central part, as long as input a
values.valid: only fully overlapping lags: length |Na − Nb| + 1

params.about: Whether to divide by √(Ea·Eb) so values lie in [−1, 1]

values.no: raw sums of products: the scale depends on the signal levels
values.yes: correlation coefficient: 1 means the same shape at that lag

title: Correlation

params.name: rule

values.bayes: BayesShrink: λ = σ²/σx per level, adapts to the signal
values.minimax: Donoho–Johnstone minimax threshold: milder than the universal one
values.sure: SureShrink: λ minimises Stein's unbiased risk estimate per level
values.visu: VisuShrink: λ = σ√(2 ln N), removes nearly all noise but oversmooths

params.about: Shrinkage function: how coefficients change relative to λ

values.hard: hard: |y| ≤ λ → 0, the rest kept; less bias, more residual noise
